description_short.value: Ghanaian universal bank majority-owned by France's Societe Generale group, which agreed in October 2026 to sell its stake to Morocco's Attijariwafa Bank.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Societe Generale Ghana PLC 2025 Annual Report (GSE PR 061/2026, corporate information and report of the directors) and GSE PR 395/2026 (Societe Generale group press release of 1 October 2026 on the sale to Attijariwafa Bank)

description_full.value: Societe Generale Ghana PLC is licensed by the Bank of Ghana as a universal bank, serving retail and corporate customers through about 40 branches and outlets. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, along with leasing and consumer credit. The French Societe Generale group owns 60.22% of its shares through its wholly owned SG Financial Services Holding. On 1 October 2026 the group signed an agreement to sell that whole stake: Attijariwafa Bank, a pan-African banking group, would buy 55.22% and Ghana's Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) a further 5%, subject to regulatory approval. Its only subsidiary, SSB Investments Limited, once managed the bank's equity investments but has been inactive since they were sold off after 2003. The company was incorporated in February 1975 and has been listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange since 13 October 1995. Its head office is on Ring Road Central in Accra. After losses on the 2022 domestic debt exchange it paid no dividends for 2022 or 2023. Profit after tax peaked at GHS 551 million in 2024 and fell to GHS 397 million in 2025 as the cedi strengthened.
